title: Dual distribution
question: Should Doubt ship as both an Agent Skill and a command-line package?
verdict: Keep the Agent Skill and deterministic CLI as two surfaces of one evidence contract.

nodes.label: Current position
nodes.text: Ship both the Agent Skill and CLI.

nodes.label: Agent-facing workflow
nodes.text: The skill tells an agent when to create a map and requires it to preserve disagreement and exact source regions.

nodes.label: Deterministic surface
nodes.text: The package exposes a doubt executable and includes the same skill payload in its published files.

nodes.label: Emerging distribution
nodes.text: The discovery builder targets schema version 0.2 and packages a root-level portable skill archive.

nodes.label: Qualification
nodes.text: The two surfaces are useful only if they continue to enforce one canonical evidence contract.

nodes.label: Missing evidence
nodes.text: No installation telemetry or cross-platform user sample yet shows which surface people actually retain.

edges.note: The Agent Skill supplies the judgment workflow that a validator alone cannot.
The CLI supplies reproducible validation and rendering after an agent proposes the map.
Supporting an emerging draft distribution format adds maintenance before adoption is proven.
Surface count must not create divergent schemas or claims.
Observed retention by surface would determine whether dual distribution is worth maintaining.

sources.title: Doubt Agent Skill
sources.excerpt: Build a Doubt map when a consequential question has competing claims or meaningful missing evidence. Preserve disagreement instead of compressing it into a single confident paragraph.

sources.title: doubt-ai package manifest
sources.excerpt: The package maps the doubt executable to bin/doubt.js and includes action, benchmarks, examples, source, and skill directories in the published artifact.

sources.title: Agent Skill discovery builder
sources.locator: Section: index schema and archive construction
sources.excerpt: The builder emits a schema_version 0.2 discovery index, a sha256 digest, and a root-level tar.gz archive containing the canonical skill payload.
